stages.title: Side goal: repeatable benchmark
stages.goal: Give every performance goal one shared measuring tool: fixed saves, recorded orders and a scripted camera, with per-tick CRCs proving each run matched. Runs alongside the main stages; nothing on the road to playable waits for it.
stages.exit: A player or session can start the benchmark from the game or the command line, get a report, and see a clear flag when a run is not comparable with its baseline.

stages.title: Graphics & Performance
stages.goal: Measure first, then spread and parallelise the heavy work without breaking determinism. Measuring can start at any time. The parallel work waits for the AI and tactical groups, so the edits do not clash. Also the FSR and XeSS upscalers, port features that are off by default (moved here from Stage 8 · Port features on 2026-11-21, Gabriel).
stages.exit: Big AI updates no longer land on a single tick, and results stay identical at any thread count. FSR and XeSS each pass their own exit test with the switch on, and every golden passes unchanged with it off.

stages.title: Parity and full QA pass
stages.goal: Compare the finished port against base Forces of Corruption by behaviour (Q4), then run one deeper playtest and QA pass over the whole game instead of chasing single captures (QAFULL). The mod boxes Q5, Q6 and MODC moved to Stage 9 on 2026-11-19; Stage 7 (Full QA pass) was merged in on 2026-11-21 (Gabriel).
stages.exit: The behaviour comparison against base Forces of Corruption passes within tolerance, a fresh frame-by-frame capture review has no open P0 or P1 item, and every unconfirmed check from the earlier playtests has a verdict.

stages.title: Mod system
stages.goal: All mod-system work in one stage (Gabriel, 2026-11-19: Stage 6's mod boxes Q5, Q6 and MODC moved in; Stage 10, the unified mod system refactor, stays its own finished stage). Make most, if not all, installed Forces of Corruption mods play as in retail: generated coverage ledgers (tags, Lua bindings, story rewards, AI tokens, asset formats), retail value rules for every XML loader, no port limit below retail, asset salvage settled against retail, mod stacks from modinfo.json, and a graded corpus of every installed mod (legacy docs/MOD_COMPAT_DESIGN.md and the 2026-11-17 mod audit).
stages.exit: Every mod in the reference set of docs/MODS.md passes its checklist (mcx9; MODC folded into MCX6 2026-11-20); the corpus runner grades every installed workshop mod and local submod stack G3 (or lower only for retail-equivalent or out-of-scope reasons), and the four reference mods G4.
